questions.question_text: Infants:

options.text: By 3 months can recognize photographs of their mothers and prefer pictures of them to pictures of strangers
By 5 months can remember faces of strangers
Appear to be born with perceptual mechanisms that are already tuned to the properties of human speech
Can discriminate among tastes and among odours soon after birth
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: There are sensitive periods optimal for a particular type of development.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about newborns' preferences for sounds, except:

options.text: They prefer speech sounds over instrumental music
They prefer heartbeats over male voices
They prefer female voices over male voices
They prefer their mother's voice to other women's voices
They prefer their father's voice to other men's voices

correct_answer.text: They prefer their father's voice to other men's voices

correct_answers.text: They prefer their father's voice to other men's voices

questions.explanation: A newborn can indicate a preference for certain sounds by sucking more vigorously on a nipple when preferred sounds are played through an earphone.

questions.question_text: Which age group is correctly paired with Piaget's stage of cognitive development?

options.text: Birth to 2 years–Sensorimotor
2 to 5 years–Preoperational
5 to 9 years–Concrete operational
9 years and over–Formal operational
All of the above

correct_answer.text: Birth to 2 years–Sensorimotor

correct_answers.text: Birth to 2 years–Sensorimotor

questions.explanation: Preoperational, 2 to 7 years; concrete operational, 7 to 11 years; formal operational, 11 years and over.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about Piaget's stages of cognitive development, except:

options.text: Object permanence is achieved at the sensorimotor stage
Egocentrism is characteristic of the preoperational stage
Authoritarian morality is achieved in the concrete operational stage
Laws of conservation and reversibility are achieved in the concrete operational stage
In the formal operational stage, children can test a hypothesis systematically.

correct_answer.text: Authoritarian morality is achieved in the concrete operational stage

correct_answers.text: Authoritarian morality is achieved in the concrete operational stage

questions.explanation: Authoritarian morality is achieved in the preoperational stage.

questions.question_text: All of the following are characteristic of Piaget's preoperational stage, except:

options.text: Animistic thinking
Creationism
Phenomenalistic causality and syncretism
Precausal reasoning
Symbolization

correct_answer.text: Symbolization

correct_answers.text: Symbolization

questions.explanation: Symbolization expressed in mental symbols and words occurs in the sensor motor stage. Animism attributes life and feelings to inanimate objects. Phenomenalistic causality claims that events that occur together are thought to cause one another.

questions.question_text: All of the following are behavioural dimensions identified by Thomas and Chess (1977) in infants, except:

options.text: Activity level
Rhythmicity
Quality of mood
Attention span and persistence
Insecure attachment

correct_answer.text: Insecure attachment

correct_answers.text: Insecure attachment

questions.explanation: The nine behavioural dimensions identified by Thomas and Chess include approach or withdrawal, adaptability, intensity of reaction, threshold of responsiveness, and distractibility, in addition to a, b, c and d.

questions.question_text: All of the following attachment theorists' names are correctly paired with their observations, except:

options.text: Harry Harlow–Social learning and the effects of social isolation in surrogate-reared monkeys
John Bowlby–Attachment behaviour
Mary Ainsworth–Transitional object
Rene Spitz–Developmental retardation accompanies maternal rejection and neglect
Margaret Mahler–Separation individualization

correct_answer.text: Mary Ainsworth–Transitional object

correct_answers.text: Mary Ainsworth–Transitional object

questions.explanation: Ainsworth, expanding on Bowlby's observations, confirmed that attachment serves the purpose of reducing anxiety and observed that inanimate objects also serve as a secure base; however, Donald Winnicott called these inanimate objects transitional objects.

questions.question_text: Regarding attachment in infants, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Monotropic attachment (to one individual) is less common than polytropic attachment
Attachment usually takes place from mother to infant
The attachment process can start soon after birth
The attachment process takes an average of 3 months to complete
Imprinting commonly occurs in primates

correct_answer.text: The attachment process can start soon after birth

correct_answers.text: The attachment process can start soon after birth

questions.explanation: Monotropic attachment (to one individual, usually the mother) is more common than polytropic attachment.

questions.question_text: Attachment behaviours:

options.text: Start to occur at the age of 6 months
Are signs of distress shown by the child when separated from his/her attachment figure
Include being more playful and talkative in the presence of the attachment figure
Decrease visibly by 3 years
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Attachment behaviour is an infant's tendency to seek closeness to particular people and to feel more secure in their presence.

questions.question_text: Insecure attachment:

options.text: Is chronic clinginess and ambivalence towards the mother
May be a precursor to childhood emotional disorders
May be a precursor to school refusal
May be a precursor to agoraphobia starting in adolescence
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Insecure attachment can be avoidant or ambivalent.

questions.question_text: Regarding abnormalities in attachment:

options.text: Avoidant attachment caused by rejection by the mother may be a precursor to poor social functioning and aggression in later life
The rate of disappearance of separation anxiety varies with the child's temperament
Acute separation reaction described by Bowlby includes stages of protest, despair and detachment
Maternal deprivation can lead to developmental language delay
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Studies suggest that children who are securely attached by the time they enter their second year are better equipped to cope with new experiences.

questions.question_text: Stranger anxiety:

options.text: Is shown by infants usually between the ages of 8 months and 1 year
Is identical to separation anxiety
Is more likely to appear in babies exposed to a variety of caretakers
Does not occur when the infant is in the mother's arms
All of the above

correct_answer.text: Is shown by infants usually between the ages of 8 months and 1 year

correct_answers.text: Is shown by infants usually between the ages of 8 months and 1 year

questions.explanation: Separation anxiety occurs between 10 and 18 months of age; it is related to stranger anxiety but not identical to it.

questions.question_text: The theory of separation individualization proposed by Margaret Mahler includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Periods of sleep outweigh periods of arousal in the stage of normal autism between birth and 2 months
Mother–infant is perceived as a single fused entity in the symbiosis stage between 2 and 5 months
The infant starts to draw attention away from self to the outer world in the stage of practising between 10 and 18 months
Children move away from their mothers and come back for reassurance in the stage of rapprochement between 18 and 24 months
Children are reassured by the permanence of their mother in the stage of object constancy between 2 and 5 years of age

correct_answer.text: The infant starts to draw attention away from self to the outer world in the stage of practising between 10 and 18 months

correct_answers.text: The infant starts to draw attention away from self to the outer world in the stage of practising between 10 and 18 months

questions.explanation: An infant starts to draw attention away from self to the outer world in the stage of differentiation (between 5 and 10 months), and the ability to move autonomously increases in the stage of practising (between 10 and 18 months).

questions.question_text: Regarding stages of development, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: If a child goes through the first 7 years without adequate vision, extensive permanent disability will result
Children who have not had enough exposure to language before age 6 or 7 may fail to acquire it all together

Although infants love to explore the faces of those who care for them, research has shown that they are attached not to the faces per se but to characteristics such as curved lines and movement complexity
A newborn can indicate a preference for certain sounds
According to Piaget, the process of a child's modifying the existing schema, to extend his/her theory of the world, is called assimilation

correct_answer.text: According to Piaget, the process of a child's modifying the existing schema, to extend his/her theory of the world, is called assimilation

correct_answers.text: According to Piaget, the process of a child's modifying the existing schema, to extend his/her theory of the world, is called assimilation

questions.explanation: According to Piaget, a child understanding a novel object or event, in terms of a pre-existing schema, is an example of assimilation; the process of the child's modifying the existing schema, to extend his/her theory of the world, is called accommodation.

questions.question_text: Failure to develop adequate attachments due to prolonged maternal separation can result in all of the following, except:

options.text: An indiscriminate relationship with strangers in later childhood
Development of obsessive compulsive disorder in early adulthood
Attention seeking and over-activity at school
Enuresis in later childhood
Growth retardation

correct_answer.text: Development of obsessive compulsive disorder in early adulthood

correct_answers.text: Development of obsessive compulsive disorder in early adulthood

questions.explanation: In psychoanalysis, the origin of obsessional personality is located at the anal stage of development.

questions.question_text: According to Piaget's stage theory:

options.text: If a cloth is placed over a toy that an 8-month-old is reaching for, the infant immediately stops reaching and appears to lose interest in the toy
3–4-year-olds cannot think in symbolic terms, as their words and images are not yet organized in a logical manner
Preoperational children are aware of perspectives other than their own
Concrete operational thinking is dominated by visual impressions
Adolescent thinking is characterized by egocentrism

correct_answer.text: If a cloth is placed over a toy that an 8-month-old is reaching for, the infant immediately stops reaching and appears to lose interest in the toy

correct_answers.text: If a cloth is placed over a toy that an 8-month-old is reaching for, the infant immediately stops reaching and appears to lose interest in the toy

questions.explanation: 3–4-year-olds can think in symbolic terms, and by about 18 months to 2 years they start using symbols.

questions.question_text: At the age of 2 years normal children:

options.text: Can refer to self by name and use pronouns
Can express emotions like guilt and envy
Can build a tower of nine or ten cubes
Can copy a circle and a cross
Can use language to describe incidents from the past

correct_answer.text: Can refer to self by name and use pronouns

correct_answers.text: Can refer to self by name and use pronouns

questions.explanation: Emotional expression develops as follows: tender affection and shame at 12–18 months; pride at 2 years; guilt and shame at 3–4 years.

questions.question_text: All of the following are associated with slower speech development, except:

options.text: Bilingual home
Larger family size
Intrauterine growth retardation
Prolonged second-stage labour
Being a twin

correct_answer.text: Bilingual home

correct_answers.text: Bilingual home

questions.explanation: Having a bilingual home is not a disadvantage.

questions.question_text: Regarding temperament, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The nine categories identified by Thomas and Chess have been found to cluster as easy child (40%), difficult child (15%) and slow-to-warm-up child (10%)
Some temperamental traits do not persist over time
According to Bates, the neural basis of temperament emerges from the limbic system and the motor cortex
Concepts of temperament can be useful in helping people solve problems
In a study Capsi and Silva showed inhibited children at the age of 3 scored high on measures of impulsivity, danger seeking, aggression, and subsequent interpersonal alienation at the age of 18

correct_answer.text: In a study Capsi and Silva showed inhibited children at the age of 3 scored high on measures of impulsivity, danger seeking, aggression, and subsequent interpersonal alienation at the age of 18

correct_answers.text: In a study Capsi and Silva showed inhibited children at the age of 3 scored high on measures of impulsivity, danger seeking, aggression, and subsequent interpersonal alienation at the age of 18

questions.explanation: In a study Caspi and Silva showed uncontrolled children at the age of 3 scored high on measures of impulsivity, danger seeking, aggression, and subsequent interpersonal alienation at the age of 18, and inhibited children scored low.

questions.question_text: Regarding moral development in children, Kohlberg's stage theory states that:

options.text: In the pre-conventional stage up to the age of 7, morality is mainly reward and punishment oriented
In the conventional stage (7–13), rules are conformed to in order to avoid the disapproval of others
In the conventional stage, laws and social rules are upheld in order to avoid the censure of authorities
The stage of post-conventional morality with social contract and ethical principle orientation may never be reached even in adulthood
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Kohlberg described six developmental stages of moral judgement categorized into three levels.

questions.question_text: Regarding social learning theory and sex typing, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Research suggests that human males are more physically aggressive than human females
Observational learning enables children to imitate same-sex adults and thereby acquire sex-typed behaviours
If a culture becomes less sex typed in ideology, children become less sex typed in their behaviour
Fathers appear to be more concerned with sex-typed behaviour than mothers are, particularly with their sons
Most 6- and 7-year-olds believe that there should be no sex-based restrictions on occupations

correct_answer.text: Most 6- and 7-year-olds believe that there should be no sex-based restrictions on occupations

correct_answers.text: Most 6- and 7-year-olds believe that there should be no sex-based restrictions on occupations

questions.explanation: Most 6- and 7-year-olds believe that there should be sex-based restrictions on occupations, as they hold more rigid opinions.

questions.question_text: Regarding social learning theory and modelling, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Aggression in children may be learned by modelling
Modelling has been shown to reduce anxiety
Modelling was found to have no aetiological association with the development of personality disorders
Fearful children become less fearful when they watch other children acting fearlessly in the same situation
It is possible to eliminate negative behaviour patterns by having a person learn alternative techniques from other role models

correct_answer.text: Modelling was found to have no aetiological association with the development of personality disorders

correct_answers.text: Modelling was found to have no aetiological association with the development of personality disorders

questions.explanation: In modelling, the person learns behaviours by observing others and it is thought to be linked to the development of personality disorders, since maladaptive behaviours can be learnt through modelling.

questions.question_text: Bandura:

options.text: Regarded reinforcement and motivational processes as components of observational learning
Proposed the concept of reciprocal determinism
Observed that, in modelling, attention is attracted by models because of their distinctiveness, success, power and prestige
Observed that people's choices of model are influenced by age, sex and similarity
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Bandura promotes the behaviourist/social learning approach.

questions.question_text: Erik Erikson suggested that:

options.text: During child development there is a trust-versus-mistrust crisis between 3 and 5 years of age
At about 1–3 years, parental over-control or children's loss of self-control will result in muscular and anal impotence and produce a sense of doubt and shame
Between 3 and 5 years of age, excessive punishment leads to the development of a too-strong superego, but with a sense of responsibility, dependability and self-discipline
Between the ages of 6 and 11, if the parents reward children's industriousness at home, a school environment that denigrates or discourages children cannot diminish their self-esteem
If an identity crisis occurs at the end of adolescence it is abnormal

correct_answer.text: At about 1–3 years, parental over-control or children's loss of self-control will result in muscular and anal impotence and produce a sense of doubt and shame

correct_answers.text: At about 1–3 years, parental over-control or children's loss of self-control will result in muscular and anal impotence and produce a sense of doubt and shame

questions.explanation: Erikson's stages of life cycle are as follows: stage 1 (birth to 1 year), trust versus mistrust is the first crisis and towards the second half of the first year an oral crisis occurs.

questions.question_text: All of the following are related to Winnicott's theory, except:

options.text: True self
Holding environment
Good-enough mother
Transitional object
Paranoid-schizoid position

correct_answer.text: Paranoid-schizoid position

correct_answers.text: Paranoid-schizoid position

questions.explanation: The paranoid-schizoid position is described by Melanie Klein.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true statements about Melanie Klein's work, except:

options.text: She viewed projection and repression as the primary defensive operations in the first months of life
She described a phenomenon of persecutory anxiety, when infants project derivatives of the death instinct onto the mother, and then fear attack from a 'bad mother'
The paranoid-schizoid position is characterized by the predominance of defence mechanism denial, splitting and primitive projective identification
In the depressive position, the mother is viewed ambivalently as having both positive and negative aspects
She developed a play technique in the psychoanalysis of children

correct_answer.text: She viewed projection and repression as the primary defensive operations in the first months of life

correct_answers.text: She viewed projection and repression as the primary defensive operations in the first months of life

questions.explanation: Melanie Klein viewed projection and introjection as the primary defensive operations in the first months of life.

questions.question_text: Regarding the oral stage of Freud's stages of psychosexual development, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It happens in approximately the first 18 months of life
Oral drives consist of two separate components: aggressive and libidinal
The aggressive components are thought to predominate in the early parts of the oral phase, whereas they are mixed with more libidinal components later
Excessive oral gratification or deprivation can result in libidinal fixations, leading to excessive optimism, narcissism and pessimism
Successful resolution of the oral phase provides a capacity to rely on others with a sense of trust and sense of self-reliance

correct_answer.text: The aggressive components are thought to predominate in the early parts of the oral phase, whereas they are mixed with more libidinal components later

correct_answers.text: The aggressive components are thought to predominate in the early parts of the oral phase, whereas they are mixed with more libidinal components later

questions.explanation: The libidinal components are thought to predominate in the early parts of the oral phase (oral erotism), whereas they are mixed with more aggressive components later (oral sadism).

questions.question_text: Regarding the anal stage of Freud's stages of psychosexual development, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It extends roughly from 1 to 5 years
Anal eroticism refers to the sexual pleasure in anal retention of faeces and in presenting them as a precious gift to parents
Anal sadism refers to the expression of aggressive wishes connected with discharging faeces as a powerful and destructive weapon
Anal characteristics and defences are most typically seen in obsessive compulsive neuroses
The urethral stage was treated by Freud as a transitional stage between anal and genital and the resolution of urethral conflicts sets the stage for budding gender identity

correct_answer.text: It extends roughly from 1 to 5 years

correct_answers.text: It extends roughly from 1 to 5 years

questions.explanation: The anal stage of Freud's stages of psychosexual development extends roughly from 1 to 3 years.

questions.question_text: In the phallic stage of Freud's stages of psychosexual development:

options.text: The penis becomes the organ of principal interest in both sexes
The lack of a penis in the female is considered as evidence of castration
Castration anxiety arises in connection with guilt over masturbation and oedipal wishes

The influences of castration anxiety and penis envy, the defences against both, and the patterns of identification that emerge from the phallic phase are the primary determinants of the development of human character
Fixations and conflicts that derive from the preceding stages cannot usually modify the oedipal resolution

correct_answer.text: Fixations and conflicts that derive from the preceding stages cannot usually modify the oedipal resolution

correct_answers.text: Fixations and conflicts that derive from the preceding stages cannot usually modify the oedipal resolution

questions.explanation: Fixations and conflicts deriving from the preceding stages can contaminate and modify the oedipal resolution.

questions.question_text: The concepts associated with Jungian theory are:

options.text: Collective unconsciousness
Archetypes and complexes
Introverts and extroverts
Individualization
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Collective unconsciousness (objective psyche) contains latent memories of our cultural, racial and phylogenetic past.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are correct, except:

options.text: Adler coined the term inferiority complex
Oral frustration and oral envy are terms used by Melanie Klein
Concepts associated with Winnicott include potential space and primary maternal preoccupation
Bion described the concept of basic assumptions
The concepts of 'container' and 'contained' and 'squiggle game' are associated with Anna Freud

correct_answer.text: The concepts of 'container' and 'contained' and 'squiggle game' are associated with Anna Freud

correct_answers.text: The concepts of 'container' and 'contained' and 'squiggle game' are associated with Anna Freud

questions.explanation: The concepts of 'container' and 'contained' are associated with Wilfred Bion.

questions.question_text: Regarding family factors in child development, which of the following is true?

options.text: Vulnerability to unstable homes is influenced by sex and girls are more affected than boys
Vulnerability to unstable homes is influenced by age and older children are more vulnerable than younger children
In childhood and adolescence, the death of a parent is associated with adverse effects, such as an increase in later emotional problems, particularly a susceptibility to depression and divorce
Evidence indicates that working mothers raise children who are less healthy than those brought up by mothers who stay at home
When home caretakers act as surrogate mothers, children usually become more attached to the caretaker than to the parent

correct_answer.text: In childhood and adolescence, the death of a parent is associated with adverse effects, such as an increase in later emotional problems, particularly a susceptibility to depression and divorce

correct_answers.text: In childhood and adolescence, the death of a parent is associated with adverse effects, such as an increase in later emotional problems, particularly a susceptibility to depression and divorce

questions.explanation: Regarding vulnerability to unstable homes, boys are more affected than girls, and older children are less vulnerable than younger ones.

questions.question_text: Regarding family factors in child development, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Single parenting has been found to have an association with increased emotional and behavioural problems in children
Having two lesbian parents has been found to have an association with increased emotional and behavioural problems in children
Large family size has been found to have an association with increased emotional and behavioural problems in children
In dysfunctional families, marital conflicts may cause the parents to use a child with problems as a scapegoat
Parental divorce is associated with an increased rate of disturbance in children, greater than following parental bereavement

correct_answer.text: Having two lesbian parents has been found to have an association with increased emotional and behavioural problems in children

correct_answers.text: Having two lesbian parents has been found to have an association with increased emotional and behavioural problems in children

questions.explanation: Having two lesbian parents was not identified as a harmful factor.

questions.question_text: Death of a parent leads to:

options.text: Increased functional enuresis and increased temper tantrums in young children
Increased sleep disturbance in older children
Depressive reactions in girls
Impaired school performance
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Increased temper tantrums and prolonged bereavement reactions occur.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about family functioning and parenting are true, except:

options.text: An association has been established between child psychiatric disorders and exposure to family discord
Rutter described four patterns of family interaction: enmeshment, overprotection, rigidity and lack of conflict resolution
Authoritative parenting leads to good peer and parental relationships
With authoritarian parenting, boys may be more aggressive and girls less motivated
With indulgent parenting, children are often positive but can be immature and the lack of authority may lead to increased aggressive behaviour

correct_answer.text: Rutter described four patterns of family interaction: enmeshment, overprotection, rigidity and lack of conflict resolution

correct_answers.text: Rutter described four patterns of family interaction: enmeshment, overprotection, rigidity and lack of conflict resolution

questions.explanation: Erikson's stages of life cycle are as follows: stage 1 (birth to 1 year), trust versus mistrust is the first crisis and towards the second half of the first year an oral crisis occurs.

questions.question_text: All of the following are recognized sequelae of sexual abuse in children, except:

options.text: Eating disorders
Depression
Paranoid reactions and mistrust
Neurological impairment
Borderline personality disorder

correct_answer.text: Neurological impairment

correct_answers.text: Neurological impairment

questions.explanation: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and increased drug and alcohol abuse also occur.

questions.question_text: All of the following are recognized sequelae of physical abuse in children, except:

options.text: Borderline personality disorder
Depression
Dissociation
Delayed language development
Eating disorder

correct_answer.text: Eating disorder

correct_answers.text: Eating disorder

questions.explanation: Neurological impairment is associated with physical abuse, whereas eating disorders are associated with sexual abuse.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about development of fears in childhood are true, except:

options.text: Fear of novel stimuli begins at 6 months, reaching a peak at 1 year
Fear of heights begins at 6–8 months
In the preschool age group, the common fears are of animals, the dark and monsters
Fear of shameful social situations begins between 6 and 11 years of age
Fears of death, failure and social gatherings dominate in adolescence

correct_answer.text: Fear of novel stimuli begins at 6 months, reaching a peak at 1 year

correct_answers.text: Fear of novel stimuli begins at 6 months, reaching a peak at 1 year

questions.explanation: Fear of novel stimuli begins at 6 months, reaching a peak at 18 months to 2 years.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about fears and dreams in childhood are true, except:

options.text: Freud proposed that displacement of fear of castration to situations symbolic of that conflict leads to development of phobias
Most 3-year-olds understand that dreams are unique to each individual
Newborns were found to have some brain activity similar to that of the dreaming state
At the age of 5–6, dreams of being killed or injured and of ghosts become prominent
Adults spend 20% of sleeping time dreaming

correct_answer.text: Most 3-year-olds understand that dreams are unique to each individual

correct_answers.text: Most 3-year-olds understand that dreams are unique to each individual

questions.explanation: At the age of 3 years, many children believe that dreams are directly shared by more than one person, but most 4-year-olds understand that dreams are unique to each individual.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about sexual development are true, except:

options.text: Over-ripeness of the ovum at fertilization is associated with a masculinizing effect on genetic females
In 80% of girls the onset of puberty is marked by pubic hair growth
Between ages 17 and 18 luteinizing hormone is frequently elevated above adult values
In adolescent boys, testosterone levels correlate with libido and are manifested by sex drive and masturbation
An increase in suprarenal androgen release (adrenarche) usually begins between the ages of 6 and 8

correct_answer.text: In 80% of girls the onset of puberty is marked by pubic hair growth

correct_answers.text: In 80% of girls the onset of puberty is marked by pubic hair growth

questions.explanation: In 80% of girls the onset of puberty is marked by breast formation and in 20% by pubic hair growth.

questions.question_text: Regarding gender identity and sexual orientation, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Gender identity is usually established by the age of 3 or 4 years and usually remains firmly established thereafter
Sexual drive exists from birth to middle childhood and increases again during adolescence
Sexual fantasy is the most important dimension in assessing homosexual orientation
Research has shown that childhood gender non-conformity is a strong indicator of genetic loading for homosexuality
In pedigree and linkage analyses of homosexual men, increased rates of homosexual orientation were found in the maternal uncles and male cousins, but not in their fathers or paternal relatives

correct_answer.text: Research has shown that childhood gender non-conformity is a strong indicator of genetic loading for homosexuality

correct_answers.text: Research has shown that childhood gender non-conformity is a strong indicator of genetic loading for homosexuality

questions.explanation: In a study Bailey and Pillard found that childhood gender non-conformity did not appear to be an indicator of genetic loading for homosexuality.

questions.question_text: All of the following include the adolescent identity statuses suggested by Marcia, except:

options.text: Adolescent turmoil
Identity achievement
Foreclosure
Moratorium
Identity diffusion

correct_answer.text: Adolescent turmoil

correct_answers.text: Adolescent turmoil

questions.explanation: Affective stability and adolescent turmoil were described by Anna Freud, Erikson, and Offer and Offer.

questions.question_text: The symptomatology of normal grief does not include:

options.text: A feeling of numbness as a result of initial shock and disbelief and denial of anger
Adopting the mannerisms and characteristics of the deceased person (identification phenomena)
Somatic symptoms, including biological symptoms of depression
Intense anger and feelings of betrayal persisting up to 6 months after bereavement
Misery and searching behaviour persisting for up to 6 months after bereavement

correct_answer.text: Intense anger and feelings of betrayal persisting up to 6 months after bereavement

correct_answers.text: Intense anger and feelings of betrayal persisting up to 6 months after bereavement

questions.explanation: Intense anger and feelings of betrayal persisting beyond 6 weeks after bereavement are regarded as an abnormal grief reaction.

questions.question_text: About the grief reaction, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The initial stages of grief described by Parks include alarm and numbness
In the stage of pining described by Parks, illusions or hallucinations of the deceased may occur
In the depressive stage of grief described by Parks, disorganization and despair occur
If a parent/caregiver dies before the development of attachment behaviour, grief reaction is still seen in babies
Grief reactions of any duration, considered to be abnormal because of their form or content, are classified under adjustment disorders in ICD-10

correct_answer.text: If a parent/caregiver dies before the development of attachment behaviour, grief reaction is still seen in babies

correct_answers.text: If a parent/caregiver dies before the development of attachment behaviour, grief reaction is still seen in babies

questions.explanation: If a parent/caregiver dies before the development of attachment behaviour, grief reaction is not seen in babies.

questions.question_text: According to Erikson:

options.text: Initiative versus guilt is the dominant theme between 3 and 5 years
Intimacy versus isolation dominates in adolescence
Industry versus inferiority dominates in early adulthood
Generativity versus stagnation is the dominant theme after 65 years of age
All of the above are true

correct_answer.text: Initiative versus guilt is the dominant theme between 3 and 5 years

correct_answers.text: Initiative versus guilt is the dominant theme between 3 and 5 years

questions.explanation: Erikson's stages of life cycle are as follows: stage 1 (birth to 1 year), trust versus mistrust is the first crisis and towards the second half of the first year an oral crisis occurs.

questions.question_text: Regarding intelligence tests, all of the following are true, except:
